profile.address: Agnew Road, Agnew, Santa Clara, Santa Clara County, California, 95054
profile.reading:
This building is mapped as an Amazon Web Services facility on Agnew Road in the Agnew area of Santa Clara, Santa Clara County, California, part of the long established Silicon Valley data center market. AWS has not published a street address, opening date, floor area, or IT power rating that this research could confirm applies specifically to this mapped location, and no source found this session ties the Agnew Road tag to a named AWS project.

Two separately documented Amazon data center projects exist nearby in Santa Clara, and neither could be confirmed as a match to this exact coordinate. The better known one sits about three miles north at 2305 Mission College Boulevard. Filed by developer Oppidan Investment Company under City of Santa Clara file numbers PLN2019-14213 and CEQ2020-01077, that project proposes demolishing a 358,000 square foot office and research building and replacing it with two three story data center buildings totaling roughly 490,000 square feet, a 278,526 square foot first phase and a 211,425 square foot second phase, plus a new city owned electrical substation on the parcel's north side. Trade press coverage reports each building carrying 49.5 megavolt amperes of power capacity, with Silicon Valley Power building a new 60 kilovolt Freedom Circle Junction substation and roughly 9 megavolt amperes of interim service to support it, a roughly 26 month construction effort priced near 5.4 million dollars for the substation work alone, paid for by Oppidan on Amazon's behalf. Amazon is reported to have purchased that site in 2020 for about 100 million dollars. Separately, under California Energy Commission docket 19-SPPE-05, filed November 25, 2019 for a small power plant exemption, the same Mission College Boulevard project's backup power is described as 43 diesel fired emergency generators at 2.5 megawatts each plus two smaller house power units, a combined 78.1 megawatts of standby generation. The City of Santa Clara's own project listing marks this file archived, with a development review hearing dated August 2020 and no later public update confirming final approval or completion.

A second, unrelated Amazon transaction closed roughly three miles further south, where Amazon paid 237.8 million dollars for a 747,424 square foot former Owens Corning insulation factory site at 960 Central Expressway near San Jose Mineta International Airport, land a previous developer had proposed building out with warehouse or data center space before Amazon's purchase. That site's later use has not been confirmed as a data center in any source reviewed this session.

None of these three locations, the Mission College Boulevard project, the Central Expressway acquisition, or this Agnew Road point, has been confirmed by this research as the same building, and readers should treat the two better documented projects as regional context for Amazon's overall Santa Clara footprint rather than as facts about this specific mapped structure. Santa Clara's data center growth generally has taken the form of redevelopment of existing office, laboratory, or light industrial buildings rather than greenfield construction, reflecting the city's largely built out land supply, and Silicon Valley Power, the city's municipal electric utility, has separately stated that data centers already account for a majority of its total electricity sales.
profile.capacity_note: Not published for this specific mapped location. The City of Santa Clara's own project records disclose square footage for a separate, large data center project nearby (2305 Mission College Blvd, approximately 490,000 square feet across two buildings) that this research could not confirm corresponds to this exact registry entry.
profile.facility_note: AWS has not identified this specific building by name, construction date, or function in any source found for this page. Its correspondence to the City of Santa Clara's Mission College Blvd project record is not independently confirmed beyond general proximity and Amazon's separately reported acquisition of a former factory site in Santa Clara.
profile.research_note: Verified and rewritten 2026-09-06. Prior draft named the banned aggregators Baxtel and DataCenterMap directly in the public reading text and contained a semicolon, both house-style violations, now removed. Fresh research this session pulled the DCD article on Amazon's 960 Central Expressway acquisition, the DCD article on the Silicon Valley Power substation for the Mission College Blvd project, the CEC docket 19-SPPE-05 page, and the City of Santa Clara's own PLN2019-14213 project listing, all allowed source types. None of these establishes a confirmed match to this row's Agnew Road coordinate, so the reading presents both known nearby Amazon projects explicitly as unconfirmed regional context rather than asserting either is this building, consistent with the honesty requirement over completeness.
profile.regional_context: Santa Clara and the broader Silicon Valley corridor form one of the oldest commercial data center markets in the United States, hosting dozens of facilities from many colocation and cloud operators, including Digital Realty, Equinix, CoreSite, and Switch, in addition to Amazon and other hyperscalers. Silicon Valley Power, the City of Santa Clara's municipal electric utility, serves much of the city's data center load, and the city has separately weighed grid capacity constraints against new data center development in its own planning documents. Land in Santa Clara is largely built out, so new data center projects in the city frequently take the form of redevelopment of existing office, laboratory, or light industrial buildings, as in the Mission College Blvd project referenced above, rather than greenfield construction of the kind seen in Virginia, Ohio, or Oregon.

reading.body:
AWS has mapped a facility on Agnew Road in Santa Clara, but the operator has not published a street address, opening date, floor area, or power rating for this specific location. City of Santa Clara project records show a separate large data center development at 2305 Mission College Blvd, filed under a developer entity, proposing approximately 490,000 square feet across two buildings, but this research could not confirm whether that project corresponds to the Agnew Road coordinate. Santa Clara sits in Silicon Valley, one of the oldest commercial data center markets in the United States, where new projects typically redevelop existing office or industrial buildings rather than greenfield sites, constrained by both land availability and municipal grid capacity.

Because AWS has not disclosed power capacity for this facility, its contribution to Silicon Valley's AI infrastructure cannot be quantified from published sources. The City of Santa Clara's municipal utility, Silicon Valley Power, manages grid access for the region's data center load and has raised capacity constraints in planning documents, making grid availability rather than real estate the binding factor for new development in this area.

This mapped location ranks 12th among California's published-capacity facilities but contributes zero to the state's disclosed 365 megawatts, since the operator has not published a figure. California has 103 mapped data centers but only 11 with disclosed power ratings, making this facility representative of the vast majority: real estate identified but power opaque to public analysis.
